topic_and_scope: Analysis of Malawi's 2022–2023 cholera outbreak within the context of tropical cyclone Freddy, focusing on how climate-related disasters affect water, sanitation, and health systems, including vaccine campaigns, humanitarian response, and implications for SDG targets.
main_themes: Disaster-climate events and cholera dynamics: temporal and geographic coupling of floods/cyclones with cholera incidence and mortality.
WASH and health system vulnerability: damage to latrines, boreholes, facilities, and supply chains that exacerbate disease risk post-disaster.
Humanitarian response and vulnerable populations: distribution of services with a gender- and age-biased burden, especially for women and under-5 children in IDP camps.
main_findings: Cyclone Freddy’s floods were temporally associated with immediate increases in cholera cases and deaths in Nsanje and Chikwawa, suggesting flood-related disruptions to WASH and health services elevate cholera risk.

Extensive damage to WASH and health infrastructure (e.g., 63 health facilities damaged; 90,809 latrines collapsed; 944,784 people lacking WASH access) and large internally displaced populations contributed to heightened vulnerability, with pronounced impacts on women and under-5 children.

key_gaps.description: Inadequate and poorly maintained WASH infrastructure (latrines, boreholes, piped water) contributing to persistent cholera risk after floods, with low household latrine quality and coverage.

Lack of district-specific, proactive disaster risk reduction planning and preparedness (e.g., anticipatory vaccination, targeted WASH reinforcement) as current approaches are largely reactive rather than proactive.

future_directions.title: Implement district-specific disaster risk reduction plans using WHO DRRM framework
future_directions.rationale: The study highlights district-level variability in cholera risk and disaster impact, with Nsanje, Chikwawa, and other southern districts bearing the brunt. A formal district-level risk assessment and DRRM plan, developed with local authorities and communities, would enable proactive measures before and during flood seasons. Steps include conducting hazard and vulnerability mapping, establishing district DRRM committees, allocating budget lines for rapid deployment, and performing simulation exercises to test response workflows.

future_directions.title: Rebuild and sustain flood-resilient WASH infrastructure with maintenance programs
future_directions.rationale: Mass latrine collapse and borehole damage directly undermine disease prevention and safe water access. A program to upgrade latrines to flood-resilient designs, restore and maintain boreholes, and implement community-based WASH management is needed. Concrete next steps include baseline WASH audits, procurement of durable facilities, community maintenance brigades, and a monitoring system for functionality and water quality.

future_directions.title: Preposition and optimize coverage of Oral Cholera Vaccines in high-risk districts
future_directions.rationale: OCV campaigns reached 62% of targeted populations in selected districts, with uneven district performance. Proactive stockpiling, cold-chain strengthening, and pre-season vaccination campaigns in high-risk districts (e.g., Nsanje, Chikwawa, Thyolo, Mangochi) could avert outbreaks following floods. Actions include establishing pre-positioned vaccine caches, rapid-response vaccination teams, and integration with WASH and health-systems planning.

future_directions.title: Establish integrated, real-time disease and disaster surveillance systems
future_directions.rationale: Linkages between WASH disruptions and cholera trends require timely visualization and cross-sector data sharing. A real-time, GIS-enabled surveillance platform linking health, WASH, and disaster management data will enable early detection and targeted interventions. Next steps: formal data-sharing agreements, standardized case definitions, dashboards, and regular joint reviews with district and national authorities.

future_directions.title: Deliver gender-responsive, child-centered humanitarian interventions
future_directions.rationale: Findings show a skew toward women and under-5 children in humanitarian service uptake, with gender-based vulnerabilities and child health needs magnified during disasters. Interventions should include GBV risk mitigation, female- and child-led shelter and WASH initiatives, privacy-protective health services, and targeted vaccination and nutrition programs for PLW and young children. Implement with dedicated monitoring for gender and age-disaggregated outcomes.

future_directions.title: Strengthen health system surge capacity and supply-chain resilience
future_directions.rationale: Damage to 63 health facilities and disrupted medical supplies impeded care delivery during disasters. Build surge capacity through mobile clinics, expandable stockpiles of essential medicines and vaccines, fuel reserves, and renewable-energy power solutions. Actions include regional distribution hubs, stock-tracking systems, and routine drills to ensure continuity of essential services during emergencies.

future_directions.title: Institutionalize proactive risk communication and community engagement
future_directions.rationale: Non-adherence to evacuation directives and widespread open-defecation behaviors indicate gaps in risk communication. A proactive, culturally tailored risk communication strategy engaging local leaders, schools, religious groups, and community health workers can improve WASH practices, evacuation compliance, and uptake of vaccination and health services. Next steps: develop messaging in local languages, test with communities, and monitor changes in knowledge, attitudes, and practices.
